title: Pascal Minus-One GCD
status: Palomar verified · novelty audit in progress
headline: Lean/Mathlib formalisation complete and Palomar verified; final source-level novelty and priority audit in progress.
description: This project studies $G(N;m)=\gcd\{\binom Nk:0<k<N,\ m\mid k\}$. The repository formally proves the $p\equiv-1\pmod m$ valuation theorem, the complementary $p\equiv1\pmod m$ branch, a common prime-power scaling theorem, and complete prime-by-prime valuation corollaries for $m=3,4,6$. A source-level literature audit through September 2026 found substantial overlap with McTague's known plus-one theorem and same-residue subfamilies, but located no equivalent prior theorem for the full minus-one classification, including its mixed-parity and general $p=m-1$ cases. A final novelty and priority audit is now being conducted before paper drafting and arXiv submission.
verification: Lean-verified theorem layer: minus-one valuation, plus-one valuation, scaling, and complete modulus 3, 4 and 6 valuation corollaries. Project Lean sources have zero explicit sorry, admit, or replacement axiom declarations; CI checks the build, regression tests, reference sweep, and zero-sorry gate. Palomar registry entry: PALOMAR-2026-09-25-000017, version 1.
attribution: John Fairfax-Ball maintains the repository and its Lean formalisation. Mathlib supplies Kummer's theorem and supporting digit machinery. McTague's 2017 work gives the plus-one theorem for the same restricted gcd family, covers same-residue minus-one subfamilies for p>m, and records the m=3, p=2 valuation-2 example. The September 2026 source-level audit located no equivalent prior theorem for the full minus-one classification; a final novelty and priority audit is in progress, so the repository continues to avoid an unconditional first or priority claim.
